build: version 1.0, eight D64 images (archive.org d64_Pool_of_Radiance_v1.0_1988_SSI_Disk_1_of_4_Side_A); BOOT prints "POOL OF RADIANCE, VERSION 1.0"

comments.text: The adventure module's jump table, the same three entries every module has at $0800: $0800 its start (dungeon_init), which the linker calls with JSR $0800 at $2BB5; $0803 its redraw (redraw_view), which LIBRARY's jump table passes on from $2C90; $0806 frame_view, which nothing in the adventure module's snapshots calls.

Starts the module, and starts it again after a script loads a new area (NEWECL, $203E). Keeps the stack pointer in $03BF, so that a command that leaves the module can drop everything and return to the linker; offers ITEMS and EXIT on the VIEW screen ($6EF7 = $11) and READY, TRADE and DROP among the item actions ($6EF8 = $0D); clears the money of NPCs (npc_money); points LIBRARY's frame call at $48C7 to this module's draw_box_corners ($11BE); starts the game's interrupt with its music; puts the Search flag back from its saved copy ($6DDE to $6DCA).
Loads the area's files: in a 3D area ($49E6 not zero) load_3d_area and the party's place from the saved game, outdoors load_overland.

Then clears the text delay ($03FC) and $49E5, forces the next redraw to install the character set ($6DDF) and recolour the walls ($6DDB = $FF), draws the screen's three frames, carries on a script that a fight interrupted (resume_script), runs the area script's start entry ($9910, run_start_script) and the one that follows a camp ($990C, run_camp_return).
$6DDD counts the restarts a script asked for (NEWECL): with one pending, the module goes straight into MOVE (command 0) instead of showing the menu.

The Adventure Menu: the menu bar MOVE VIEW CAST AREA ENCAMP SEARCH LOOK (show_menu_bar), the party list on the right, the view and the status line. A choice is called through the self-modified JSR at $08A4 from the tables at $08B7 (low bytes) and $08BE (high bytes); up and down move the party cursor (party_cursor) and the left arrow is refused. Afterwards the bar's cursor ($6EE6) goes back to the place it was at ($2B47), or to the first item when the bar has become shorter than that ($6E93 items).
The operand of the Adventure Menu's JSR at $08A4: the low byte of the chosen command's routine, from menu_handlers ($08B7).
The high byte of the Adventure Menu's call, from $08BE.

The seven Adventure Menu commands' routines, low bytes here and high bytes at $08BE: MOVE $08F4, VIEW $11EA, CAST $10A1, AREA $0CFD, ENCAMP $10A6, SEARCH $7A91 (in DUNGEON2: it toggles the Search flag) and LOOK $111F.
The high bytes of menu_handlers.
Takes the step: keeps the square the party leaves in $49F0/$49F1, moves one square in the facing direction (step_forward, $C01E), then falls into pass_step_time.
The time a step takes: 1 minute, or 10 with Search on (step_minutes, by $6DCA), added to the clock (add_minutes); then a pause, the step sound (sound 8) and the lower window cleared.
Minutes per step: 1 normally, 10 with Search on.
The square ahead for each facing, used by check_leave_block: the change across for north, east, south and west (0, +1, 0, -1), then the change down at $08F0 (-1, 0, +1, 0).

MOVE. Outdoors it is the overland move (overland_move). In a 3D area: runs the square's script ($9904, run_square_script), then reads the keys or the joystick: I or up steps forward, J or left turns left, K or right turns right, M or down steps back with the facing kept (turn round, step, turn round again: $2B7F counts the turn); RETURN, the left arrow or the fire button alone ($03F0 = $0F) end the command. A step that is blocked plays sound 9 instead. The square's script runs again after every step, blocked or not, but not after a turn.

Before a step: the step sound, check_leave_block, then the step script ($9900, run_step_script), which may stop the step or move the party elsewhere. If there is a wall on the side faced, open_door deals with it. Returns carry set when the step is blocked ($6DC9).
Adds A to the facing (-1 left, +1 right, +2 round) and keeps it to 0-3; X the new facing.
Prints the Adventure Menu bar from adventure_menu_text ($0DC3) with every command offered, except AREA when the area forbids its map ($49FB not zero).
MOVE's prompt: blanks the menu bar and prints message 4, "I,J,K,M, RETURN OR BUTTON", on it, then the status line.
Sets the text window to the status lines under the view (status_window_edges).
The status window's edges: columns 17 to 39, rows 14 and 15.

The status line under the view: the way the party faces (N, E, S or W, messages 15-18 from facing_letters) in a 3D area or OUTDOORS (message 34), the time as hours, a colon, tens of minutes and minutes ($49C9, $49C8, $49C7), then, where the area allows it ($49FB zero), the party's square as two numbers, across and down; and SEARCH (message 27) when Search is on in a 3D area.
The message numbers of N, E, S and W, by facing.

Redraws the view. Installs a changed character set first (install_charset); in a 3D area: GDRIVE's view_init ($C000), the walls' colour for the square (set_wall_colour), the view's frame, then draw_view through gdrive_call with the KERNAL's interrupt in place. Outdoors: reloads the overland squares (slot 4) when bit 7 of $6E17 is set, sets the overland colours ($D022 = 15, $D023 = 5) and calls $C04E, which outdoors is the overland driver GDRIVE00's draw routine (in a 3D area $C04E is GDRIVE01's wall_ahead); then shows the party's marker, a sprite picture chosen by the direction last walked (overland_icons), stepping through the picture's three images, one each redraw ($2B60, as the distance $6DC0, with the cell at overland_frames in $6DBF).
The party marker's picture outdoors: 3 after a move north to south-east (directions 0-3), 30 after one south to north-west (4-7), by $033D, the last direction, over four.
The cell the marker's sprites are placed by ($6DBF) for each of its three images: 0, 3 and 8, the middle cell at each distance (sprite_offsets gives all three no shift).

Moving outdoors, eight ways: runs the square's script ($9904), shows the status line and the prompt "1-8, RETURN OR BUTTON" (message 24); keys 1 to 8 or the joystick (overland_directions) give a direction, 1 north and on clockwise, and RETURN, the left arrow or the fire button end it. The step script ($9900) may stop the move; otherwise GDRIVE00 ($C027) moves the party, the new square goes into $49C3/$49C4 and the clock gains a step's minutes and twelve hours (add_half_day).
The eight-way direction for each joystick reading (its low four bits, 0 for a direction pressed): up 0, up-right 1, right 2, down-right 3, down 4, down-left 5, left 6, up-left 7.
Copies the party's overland square ($49C3 across, $49C4 down) into $FB/$FC for GDRIVE00.
Copies $FB/$FC back to the party's overland square ($49C3/$49C4).
Message 0, "THE PARTY ATTACKS": the encounter's outcome when the party chooses COMBAT and the monsters do not.
Messages 1 and 2, "A BATTLE BEGINS": the encounter's outcome when the monsters attack (1) or both sides do (2).
Message 3, "THE PARTY FLEES": the party got away from an encounter.
Message 4, "I,J,K,M, RETURN OR BUTTON": MOVE's prompt in a 3D area.
Message 5, "DEATH FOR ALL": printed by DAMAGE when no one in the party is left standing, before the game stops for good.
Message 6, "THE MONSTERS FLEE": the monsters got away from an encounter.
Messages 7 and 8, "THE MONSTERS ADVANCE": shown when the party chose ADVANCE and the monsters did not (7) as well as when only the monsters advance (8); the table gives both the one string.
Message 9, "BOTH PARTIES ADVANCE".
Message 10, "EVERYONE WAITS": neither side acted, and the encounter menu comes back.
Message 11, "THE DOOR IS LOCKED.", printed when a step meets a locked door.
Message 12, "WHAT DO YOU DO?", the question above the door menu.
Messages 13 to 15, "N": the status line's letter when the party faces north (15; 13 and 14 are not used).
Message 16, "E", facing east.
Message 17, "S", facing south.
Message 18, "W", facing west.
Message 19, "PICK SPEAKER": PARLAY's question, passed by its address ($0C2B) rather than its number.
Message 24, "1-8, RETURN OR BUTTON": the overland move's prompt.
Message 25, "THE DOOR IS STILL LOCKED.": an attempt on a door failed.
Message 26, "THE DOOR OPENS !".
Message 27, "SEARCH": shown on the status line while Search is on.
Message 28, an empty string.
Messages 20 to 23 and 29, "LOOKING ...": LOOK prints it (29); 20 to 23 are not used.
Messages 30 and 31, "EXIT", not used in this module.
Messages 32 to 34, "OUTDOORS": the status line's word outdoors (34).
Messages 35 to 38, " IS ": DAMAGE prints it (38) between a name and the condition it left them in.
Message 39, " IS HIT FOR ": DAMAGE prints it between a name and the hit points lost.
The module's 40 messages for print_line ($7A9D, in DUNGEON2), low bytes here and high bytes at $0CD5. Several numbers share a string, and some are not used.
The high bytes of message_table, $0B or $0C.

AREA, in a 3D area only: draws the map (draw_area_map), then blinks the party's square on it, a yellow party glyph (character $1C) taking turns with what the map has there, until a key or the joystick is pressed; then redraws the view.
Not called: shows the combat figures (show_combat_stats) two columns in, then the portrait (show_portrait).
Not called: clears the window and shows the top half of the character screen (show_character after its first call, $34ED) two columns in.
Not called: the party list in the main window (window_main), without the cursor.
Clears the text window and lists the party without the chosen member highlighted ($3E06).
The party list in the right-hand window (window_right), without the highlight: after a script changes a character.

Seven frames for draw_box_corners, four bytes each (left column, top row, right column, bottom row): $0D6F (23,0)-(39,11), $0D73 (23,12)-(39,22), $0D77 (0,0)-(22,22), $0D7B the view (0,0)-(16,16), $0D7F the party list (16,0)-(39,16), $0D83 the text area (0,16)-(39,23), $0D87 inside the view (2,2)-(14,14).
Not called: the frame round the whole screen (the corners at $4835) with this module's corners.
Not called: the three frames at $0D6F, $0D73 and $0D77, a layout this module does not use.
The Adventure Menu's screen: frames round the text area ($0D83), the view ($0D7B) and the party list ($0D7F).
The frame inside the view ($0D87), drawn before the 3D view.
The Adventure Menu bar for menu_bar: seven items, an empty heading, then MOVE, VIEW, CAST, AREA, ENCAMP, SEARCH and LOOK.

Adds one to the clock's figure X ($49C6 + X) and carries: each figure counts up to its limit in clock_limits and starts again at 0, carrying into the next; past the last, the year ($49CC/$49CD) goes up. Every figure that goes up is passed to count_step (DUNGEON2), which counts the days ($49EC/$49ED). Returns X, the highest figure that changed.

After the clock moves, X the highest figure that changed: for the minutes, ten minutes, hours or days (X 1 to 4) takes one off every timed effect counted in that unit, unit X-1 (0 minutes, 1 ten-minute turns, 2 hours, 3 days), through age_effects_by. Only the highest figure's unit is aged, so on a minute that carries into the ten minutes the effects counted in minutes miss their tick, and so on for each carry.

Takes A from the count of every timed effect whose unit is X: the 64 effects are the bytes at $4900 (zero for none) and $4980, whose top two bits are the unit and low six bits the count. A count that would reach zero or less is left as $01, unit 0 and count 1, for the code that ends effects to find.
Where each clock figure starts again at 0: 10 for $49C6 (a figure below minutes that this module never changes), 10 minutes, 6 tens of minutes, 24 hours, 30 days and 12 months.
Adds A minutes to the clock, one at a time, ageing the effects after each (add_time_unit, age_effects).

A step meets a wall. Its door bits on the side faced (door_state) decide: 0 a wall, and the step is blocked; 1 a door that opens, and the party walks through; 2 or 3 a locked door ($2B6D). For a locked door the module remembers the last door tried (recall_door): "THE DOOR IS LOCKED." (message 11), "WHAT DO YOU DO?" (message 12) and the door menu BASH PICKLOCK KNOCK DISPEL QUIT, with KNOCK and DISPEL only when someone has the spell memorised (door_menu_mask).

PICKLOCK: never on a type 2 door. Otherwise the best open-locks figure in the party ($2B66, from $6BA6) is tried once: a roll of 1 to 100 below it opens the door; a failure is remembered ($2B68), and the door stays shut until someone with a better figure tries.
"THE DOOR IS STILL LOCKED." (message 25), and back to the door menu.

"THE DOOR OPENS !" (message 26): the step is no longer blocked, the door bits on both sides of the wall become 1 (mark_door_open, for this square facing it and for the square beyond facing back) and the party's place is put back.

BASH, with the bash sound (sound 6) and the party's best strength ($2B67, the strength index from $6BE2). On a type 2 door: a roll of 1 to 24 below the bash_chances figure for that strength opens it. On a type 3 door: only a strength better than the last that failed ($2B69) may try, and a roll of 1 to 12 must come in under bash_hard_chances, which only strength 18/91 or more reaches.
KNOCK or DISPEL: the caster uses up the spell (use_door_spell). KNOCK always opens the door; DISPEL opens a type 3 door half the time and never a type 2.
Sets the door bits on the side faced to 1 (an open door) in the map's fourth page ($0700 + the square's number); $0F79 for the side in Y.
mark_door_open for the side in Y rather than the facing.

Takes KNOCK or DISPEL from the member who has it ($2B7A or $2B7B, by the choice in $2B7C): one off the party entry's byte for the spell's level ($6C03 plus the level from door_spell_levels, so $6C05 or $6C06) and its place in the memorised list ($6B20 + $2B6A or $2B6B) cleared, then the member stored back.
For each side 0-3 (north, east, south, west), the mask that keeps the other sides' door bits in a square's byte: $FC, $F3, $CF, $3F.
For each side, the value 1 in that side's two bits: $01, $04, $10, $40.

QUIT from the door menu (or the left arrow): unless both $2B68 and $2B67 are zero, keeps the door's square ($49CE), the best figures that failed ($49D2 picking, $49D6 bashing), the area ($49DA) and the facing ($49DE), so the same party cannot simply try again.
At a locked door: when it is the door last tried (the same square, facing and area), takes back the figures that failed there; otherwise starts afresh with none.
Read at $1008 + 2 and + 3 by use_door_spell: $100A and $100B hold 2 and 3, the levels of KNOCK and DISPEL (the two bytes before them are the end of recall_door).
The levels of KNOCK (2) and DISPEL (3), read as door_spell_levels + 2 and + 3.

Works out the door menu: the party's best open-locks figure ($6BA6) into $2B66 and best strength index ($6BE2) into $2B67 (check_party_stat), who has KNOCK (spell 31) and who DISPEL (spell 46, else spell 41), with the member in $2B7A/$2B7B and its place in the list in $2B6A/$2B6B (find_spell). Returns the menu mask: BASH, PICKLOCK and QUIT always ($13), KNOCK ($04) and DISPEL ($08) when found.
The door menu bar: five items, an empty heading, then BASH, PICKLOCK, KNOCK, DISPEL and QUIT.

For a type 2 door, by the party's best strength index (0-30, strength_index's scale): a roll of 1 to 24 must be below this to bash it open. 5 for index 0 to 6, 9 for 7 to 15, 13 for 16 to 19, 17 for 20 to 22, then 21, 22, 22, 22, 23, 23, 23 and 24.
For a type 3 door, by the strength index less 21 (0 below 22): a roll of 1 to 12 must be below this. 0, 3, 5, 7, 7, 9, 9, 11, 12, 12, so nothing below index 22 (strength 18/91) can bash it.
CAST: goes to the camp module with its magic menu wanted ($6DAB = 1), through encamp_command.

ENCAMP: clears $6DD2 and $6DD3, runs the area script's camp entry ($9908, run_camp_script), then sets the next module to 9, CAMP ($6E11), keeps the party's place (save_3d_position) and drops the stack back to the linker ($03BF).

Empties the keyboard buffer and waits for a key or the joystick (read_input). While nothing is pressed and a picture is on show ($2B79 zero), loads ANIMATE (slot 11) and runs a frame of its animation ($8403). Returns the key, with $2B79 set again.

Before a step: when the side faced has no wall, or a door that opens, works out the square ahead (step_dx_dy) and counts in $6DD5 how many of its coordinates fall outside 0-15, so the step script can tell a step off the block's edge. Returns A = $6DD5, or the door bits when the way is shut.

LOOK: treats the square as searched: Search on for the moment ($6DCA = 1), "LOOKING ..." (message 29) at the top of the menu window, ten minutes on the clock, the square's script ($9904), then the Search flag as it was ($6DDE).
The door bits of the side faced for the party's square: its byte in the map's fourth page ($0700 + the square's number, square_index) shifted down two bits per facing; 0-3 in A.

Gives the walls their colour for this square: bit 7 of the square's byte chooses $49FD or $49FE, which also goes into band_colours ($C05B, $C05C). When it differs from the colour last set ($6DDB), every colour byte of the 15 wall shapes in WALLS ($F674, 2340 bytes) whose high nibble is not zero gets it as its low nibble, with all 64 KB RAM showing.
The main window (window_main), cleared.
The lower window (window_lower), cleared.
Prints message X at the start of the text window's top row ($03F4), through print_line ($7AA3).
Moves the cursor down a row ($03CD) and returns the new row.
Plays sound A (sound_start, $BA03).

draw_box ($3C12) for the four bytes at A (low) and X (high), then character 0, the corner, in yellow at each of its four corners. LIBRARY's own frames reach it through the JSR at $48C7, which dungeon_init points here.
Puts character 0 at columns $48F2 and $48F4 of row A.
VIEW: the party member at the cursor ($6E36 indexed by $6D7B, into $6EFC) on the VIEW screen (load_member, view_menu); then the main window cleared and the frames drawn again.
wait_key, then menu_key: the next menu step or key.
Not called: shows message X of the module's table on the bottom row (show_message).
load_resource for slot X (its own file number), with the sprites off during the load (sprites_off_saving).
load_resource for slot X with the file number in A, the sprites off during the load.
Keeps the sprites' enable bits ($D015) in $2B7E and turns them off; $122E puts them back.

When the party is turned round for a backward step ($2B7F), cancels the turn back that MOVE would make afterwards and redraws, so the party is left facing what it backed into: a door, or monsters (SETUP MONSTER).
Twelve hours on the clock (add_time_unit with X = 3, twelve times, ageing the effects), then every effect counted in minutes or in ten-minute turns aged by 63, that is ended: a move outdoors.
A pause of X counts (delay, $2E23).

AREA's map, in a 3D area: an 11 by 11 piece of the 16 by 16 block around the party (five squares each side, held inside the block). For each square it reads the walls on its north and east sides (square_info with the facing set to 0 and 1) and puts a space or one of the wall characters $1D to $1F at column 3 + across and row 3 + down. The party's own square is noted in $2B75/$2B76 by match_c04b (DUNGEON2).

Starts a 3D area: its files (load_3d_files), the colours (set_colours), the view's place on the screen (set_view_place), GDRIVE's view_init ($C000), then the party's square and facing from the saved game ($49C0-$49C2).
The adventure module's colours: highlight white ($03F8 = 1), frames red ($6E35 = 2), $03F9 = 6, text green ($6E34 and $0286 = 5).
Starts outdoors: the colours (set_colours), then load_overland_files.

Loads a 3D area's files, each slot with its own file number unless noted: GDRIVE01 (slot 0, file 1), GEO (slot 2), ECL (slot 8), WALLS (slot 9), SECSET (load_secset) and the wall sets (load_wall_sets); then falls into force_recolour.
Makes the next set_wall_colour recolour the walls, whatever the colour ($6DDB = $FF).
Loads the overland's files: GDRIVE00 (slot 0, file 0), SQRPACI (slot 1), SQRDATA (slot 4), ECL (slot 8) and SECSET (load_secset).

PRINT's word wrap: the room left on the row ($03F3, the right edge, less the cursor's column $03CC) into $2B5C and the window's width into $2B7D. Finds how much of the text at $07/$08 can go on this row, up to its last space within the room or its end, and sets that length as print_string's limit ($03F6). When nothing fits and the cursor is not at the start of the row, moves to the next row (scrolling at the window's bottom) and tries again; a word as wide as the window is cut. Counts the rows printed in $2B72.
After PRINT's first row ($2B72 not zero), steps the text pointer ($07/$08) past the spaces at the start of the next.
Loads SECSET (slot 3, at $6500), the area's own characters; falls into $1405.
After a load: when a new file came in (carry set) the next redraw installs the character set ($6DDF counted up).

When $6DDF says a new character set is waiting: blanks every custom character on the screen (blank_custom_chars), then copies the 1,536 bytes at $6500 (SECSET and the three wall sets' characters) over characters $40-$FF of the character set at $D200, with all 64 KB RAM showing. Returns $FF when it did, 0 when there was nothing to do.
Puts a space in every screen position, rows 0 to 24, that holds a character $40 or above, so nothing shows half-made while the set is replaced.
block_copy with all 64 KB RAM showing: X bytes and Y pages from the address in $2B2B/$2B2C to the one in $2B2E/$2B2F.

Loads the three wall sets, last first: each WALLSET (slots 15-17, its 50 characters, at $6650, $67E0 and $6970) asks for the character set to be installed again when it is new; each WALLDEF (slots 18-20, at $8C00) is installed when it is new (install_wall_def).

Installs wall set $2B70 from the WALLDEF just loaded at $8C00: renumbers its characters for the set (renumber_wall_chars, by wall_char_offsets), copies its 780 bytes of characters, five wall shapes of 156, into WALLS (wall_char_places: $ED50, $F05C or $F368), then unpacks the colours that follow them in the file into WALLS's colour part (wall_colour_places: $F674, $F980 or $FC8C) by pushing their address and jumping into unpack_pushed (DUNGEON2).
Where each wall set's characters go in WALLS, low bytes here and high bytes at $14C2: $ED50, $F05C, $F368.
The high bytes of wall_char_places: $ED, $F0, $F3.
Where each wall set's colours go in WALLS, low bytes here and high bytes at $14C8: $F674, $F980, $FC8C.
The high bytes of wall_colour_places: $F6, $F9, $FC.

Unless the set's flag says not to ($49E7 + the set), adds A to every character number $6A or above in the 780 bytes at $8C00, so that a wall set drawn for characters $6A-$9B uses its own fifty: set 0 $6A-$9B, set 1 $9C-$CD, set 2 $CE-$FF.
What renumber_wall_chars adds for wall sets 0, 1 and 2: 0, 50 and 100.

Decodes a packed string operand (kind $80) at the instruction pointer into $9700: a count of bytes, then the bytes, read as a stream of 6-bit characters, high bit first. Character 0 is stored as it is, 1 to 31 become $41 to $5F (the letters, with $40 added) and 32 to 63 stay as they are (space, digits and signs). A zero ends it. Keeps where the string was (keep_operand_place) and returns $9700 in A/X and $4C/$4D.
Prepares GDRIVE01 for this module: no objects drawn (show_objects = 0) and the view copied to the screen at $CC7B and colour RAM at $D87B, row 3, column 3.

The area script's interpreter. Clears the lower window, keeps the stack pointer ($2B63) and empties the GOSUB stack ($6E49), then fetches each command byte at the instruction pointer ($6E47/$6E48, into $6DDC) and calls its routine through the self-modified JSR at $15A3, from command_handlers. EXIT (stop_script) ends the run by dropping the stack back to what it was here, so run_script returns to whoever called its entry.
The operand of the interpreter's JSR at $15A3: the low byte of the command's routine, from command_handlers.
The high byte of the interpreter's call, from $15E7.

The 62 script commands' routines, low bytes here and high bytes at $15E7: 0 EXIT, 1 GOTO, 2 GOSUB, 3 COMPARE, 4 ADD, 5 SUBTRACT, 6 DIVIDE, 7 MULTIPLY, 8 RANDOM, 9 SAVE, 10 LOAD CHARACTER, 11 LOAD MONSTER, 12 SETUP MONSTER, 13 APPROACH, 14 PICTURE, 15 INPUT NUMBER, 16 INPUT STRING, 17 PRINT, 18 PRINT CLEAR, 19 RETURN, 20 COMPARE AND, 21 VERTICAL MENU, 22-27 the IFs, 28 CLEAR MONSTERS, 29 PARTY STRENGTH, 30 CHECK PARTY, 31 ADDRESS OF, 32 NEW ECL, 33 LOAD FILES, 34 PARTY SURPRISE, 35 SURPRISE, 36 COMBAT, 37 ON GOTO, 38 ON GOSUB, 39 TREASURE, 40 ROB, 41 ENCOUNTER MENU, 42 GET TABLE, 43 HORIZONTAL MENU, 44 PARLAY, 45 CALL, 46 DAMAGE, 47 AND, 48 OR, 49 SPRITES OFF, 50 FIND ITEM, 51 PRINT RETURN, 52 CLOCK, 53 SAVE TABLE, 54 ADD NPC, 55 LOAD PIECES, 56 PROGRAM, 57 WHO, 58 DELAY, 59 SPELL, 60 PRINT GLYPHS, 61 CLEAR BOX. The names are this listing's, for what each routine does.
The high bytes of command_handlers.

How many operands each command takes, by command number, for skip_command: the IFs skip the next command by fetching this many. The menus, ON GOTO and ON GOSUB read a count of their own and have 0 here. Three commands' routines read one more than the table gives: SETUP MONSTER 3 (2 here), ENCOUNTER MENU 14 (13) and ADD NPC 2 (1), so any of them would be skipped wrongly after a false IF. In the scripts on the disks, as far as they decode command by command, none of the three follows an IF.

Fetches one operand. Its first byte is its kind ($6E46): 0, one byte follows, its value; 1, an address follows, the byte there (with $4C/$4D left pointing at it, for a result to be stored); 2, two bytes follow, a 16-bit value; 3 to $7F, an address, the 16-bit value there; $80, a packed string follows (decode_string), returned as $9700; $81 to $FF, an address, returned as itself (a string's or a table's place). The value comes back in A (low) and X (high).
Keeps A (low) and X (high) in $2B73/$2B74: where a string operand is, for the encounter menu's texts.
Steps the instruction pointer ($6E47/$6E48) on by one.
The byte at the instruction pointer (peek_byte), and the pointer stepped on.
Points $4C/$4D at the instruction pointer and reads the byte there.
Two bytes from the script, low first, into A and X and $4C/$4D.
Points $4C/$4D at A (low) and X (high).
An address from the script (fetch_word), then the byte there; $4C/$4D stay pointing at it.
Command 1, GOTO: the instruction pointer goes to the operand's address.
Sets the instruction pointer to A (low) and X (high).
Command 2, GOSUB: pushes the instruction pointer on the GOSUB stack ($6E4A, sixteen addresses, $6E49 its depth) and goes to the operand's address. A full stack ends the script instead.
Command 19, RETURN: pops the instruction pointer from the GOSUB stack; with the stack empty it ends the script.
Command 0, EXIT, and every way out of the interpreter: puts the stack pointer back as run_script kept it ($2B63) and returns from run_script.

Command 9, SAVE: stores the first operand in the second. A string (kind $80 and up) is copied, up to its zero, to the address the second gives; a value is written to the second operand's address, one byte, or two when its kind is 2 or more.
Copies the zero-terminated string at $51/$52 to the address in A (low) and X (high). Returns Y, its length.
Command 18, PRINT CLEAR: clears the lower window and puts the cursor at its top, then prints as PRINT.
Command 17, PRINT: a string operand is printed with word wrap (fit_word) and the text delay (set_text_delay), a row at a time, scrolling the window when full; a number is printed as a number.
Command 4, ADD: the first operand plus the second, stored in the third.
Stores A (with zero high byte) in the next operand: falls into store_result_ax.
Keeps A (low) and X (high) as the value (keep_value) and stores it in the next operand (store_value).
Fetches the next operand, a variable, and writes the value ($6E41) to its address, with the high byte ($6E42) too when its kind is 3 or more.
Command 5, SUBTRACT: the second operand less the first, stored in the third.
Command 7, MULTIPLY: the first operand times the second (eight bits each, multiply), stored in the third.
Command 6, DIVIDE: the first operand (16 bits) divided by the second (divide), stored in the third.
Command 8, RANDOM: a random number from 0 to the first operand (random_to), stored in the second.

Command 15, INPUT NUMBER: reads a line of digits only ($03B6 = $FF), at most the first operand long (input_line), and stores its value, built a digit at a time from the buffer at $9700, in the second.
Command 16, INPUT STRING: reads a line of at most the first operand's length and copies it from $9700 to the second operand's address.
Command 43, HORIZONTAL MENU: as VERTICAL MENU, with the items across the bottom row (menu_bar) and no text printed first.

Command 21, VERTICAL MENU: the first operand is the variable for the answer, then (for the vertical menu only) a text printed as PRINT CLEAR, then the number of items and each item's text. The items are copied into the working character's buffer at $6B00 as a menu for build_menu or menu_bar, the menu run until a choice is made, and the choice's number stored in the variable. The working character is then loaded again (load_member at $4415), since the menu was built over it.
Command 3, COMPARE: compares the first operand with the second, 16-bit numbers high byte first, or two strings a character at a time, and keeps the processor flags in $6E45 (keep_flags) for the IFs.
Keeps the processor's flags in $6E45, for the IFs to test.

Command 28, CLEAR MONSTERS: zeroes the monsters' character pages ($5500-$58FF) and their combat entries ($8400-$8AFF), sets $6E1E to $80, clears the treasure ($6EE7-$6EF4, with $6EF5 = $FF) and the four monster slots' bytes $6DBB-$6DBE ($FF).
The step script: clears the blocked flag ($6DC9) and runs the script from $9900, its first command. It runs before every step, and may block the step or send the party elsewhere.
At the module's start: when bit 7 of $6DD3 is set, redraws and runs the script entry at $990C.
At the module's start: runs the script entry at $9910, then keeps the area's script number ($6E1B without bit 7) in $49F2.
Runs the script entry at $9908, before the party camps (ENCAMP and CAST).
Runs the script entry at $9904: when MOVE starts in a 3D area and again after every step, taken or blocked, but not after a turn; on each overland move; and on LOOK.
Runs the script from entry X: the instruction pointer is set to the entry's address in script_entries ($9904 + 4X).

The low bytes of four of the script's entries, $9904, $9908, $990C and $9910; the high bytes, all $99, are at $1A0F. A script file (ECL, loaded at $9900) starts with five GOTO commands, four bytes each, at $9900 (the step script) and these four.
The high bytes of script_entries, all $99.

Command 36, COMBAT: keeps the instruction pointer ($6DCC/$6DCD) so the script carries on after the fight (resume_script), keeps the area's script number in $6DA9, loads character 8, the first monster, and sets the next module: 4, COM.PREP, when it has a count of monsters ($6BFB), else 5, POST.COM. Then keeps the party's place (save_3d_position) and drops the stack back to the linker.
In a 3D area, copies the party's square and facing ($C04B-$C04D) into the saved game ($49C0-$49C2).
Command 20, COMPARE AND: compares the first two operands; when they are equal the result is the comparison of the last two, otherwise the last two are skipped and the result stays not equal.

Finds room for monsters or an NPC: the last empty character slot below 8 into $03FD, the first empty one from 8 to 11 into $03FE ($80 when none), and the first empty combat entry from 8 to 63 ($8300 + 32 each) into $03FF; A = $FF when there is no entry free.
For a monster that takes several combat entries: the entry points on to the next ($6C02 = entry + 1) and is stored; the next entries point back to this one ($6C01 = entry with bit 7).

Command 11, LOAD MONSTER: loads monster file A (MON, slot 12) straight into the working character, as the next free monster character (8-11), with bit 7 of $6BB8 set and the count (the second operand) in $6BFB, then gives each of the monsters its combat entries: 1, 1, 2, 2 or 4 by its size ($6B99, monster_entry_sizes), linked together, so long as the entries ($03FF up, to 64) and character slots (to 12) last. The third operand is kept for that character at $6DB3 + slot ($6DBB-$6DBE). With no monster character free it skips the operands, but only two of its three, so the third would be read as a command.
Combat entries a monster takes by its size ($6B99 bits 0-6): 1, 1, 2, 2 and 4.
The next entry of a monster of four: entry, character slot and $6C0D one on, linked back to the head, and stored.
get_operand, called by every command.
Command 22: the next command runs only when the last comparison was equal; otherwise it is skipped (skip_command).
Command 23: the next command runs only when the last comparison was not equal.
Command 24: the next command runs only when the first value compared was the lower (carry clear).
Command 25: the next command runs only when the first value was the higher (not equal, carry set).
Command 26: the next command runs only when the first value was lower or equal.
Command 27: the next command runs only when the first value was higher or equal (carry set).
Skips the next command: fetches its number and as many operands as operand_counts gives it; $1BBE skips A operands.
The flags kept by the last comparison ($6E45) back in the processor.

Command 10, LOAD CHARACTER: an operand below $80 loads that party member as the working character (load_member); $80 and up stores the working character, its combat figures worked out again, as combat entry operand - $80, and redraws the party list.

Command 29, PARTY STRENGTH: adds up, for each member who is standing ($6C00 neither zero nor negative), five times (21 less the THAC0, from $6C0E), the full hit points ($6B76/$6B77), five points for each point of armour class below 0 ($6C0F over 60), and four times the level ($6BA0) when bit 1 of the class mask ($6BEB) is set and eight times when bit 0 is; stores a tenth of the total in the operand.
Adds A to the 16-bit value ($6E41/$6E42); $1C5D adds A and X, $1C64 only X with the carry.
Adds A (low) and X (high) to the value ($6E41/$6E42).
Adds X and the carry to the value's high byte ($6E42).
A (low) and X (high) from the pointer $4C/$4D: the address the last operand fetched pointed at.

Command 30, CHECK PARTY: the first operand names a character field (a variable, by its address) or, as a plain number, an item type; the second is a value. Over the standing members it gives the field's lowest, highest and average (into the third, fourth and fifth operands) and, in the sixth, 1 when someone's field equals the value or someone has the item (check_party_scan).
check_party_scan for the field at Y (high) and X (low), A its kind; $1CB5 with the kind already set.
check_party_stat with the field's kind already in $6E46: the field at Y (high) and X (low).

CHECK PARTY's count over members 7 to 0 who are standing: for a field (kind odd), the number of members ($6E90), the total ($6E8B/$6E8C), the lowest ($6E8D) and highest ($6E8E), and $6E8F = 1 when one equals $6E42; for an item type, $6E8F = 1 when someone has it (check_item).
$6E8F = 1 when the member has item type $6E42 (has_item_type).
Command 31, ADDRESS OF: stores the address the first operand pointed at (get_ptr_4c) in the second.
Reads the member's field at $6E43/$6E44, through armour_check.

Command 34, PARTY SURPRISE: over the standing members, stores in the first operand 1 when anyone's class mask has bit 7 set ($6BEB), and in the second the sum of three ones: when every member passes has_item_type with A = $19, when every member rolls 0-99 below their figure at $6BA8, and when any member passes has_item_type with A = $15.

Command 35, SURPRISE: from four operands a, b, c, d works out the chances (2 + d - a) and (2 + b - c), each at least 1, and rolls 0-5 against each: bit 0 of $6DCB is set when the first roll is under the first chance, bit 1 when the second is under the second.

Works out which of the nine places a monster can stand in the view are hidden by walls ($03A8-$03B0, 1 hidden): from the party's square, twelve probes (probe_moves, probe_turns) each step to a square near the front and look along one side; a wall found hides the three places that probe names (probe_cells_1-3). A hidden place then hides those behind it (cell_hides), and places 4 and 5 are always hidden. The party's place is kept and put back (save_position).

find_hidden_cells's RTS, and the byte before cell_hides, which is read from $1E79 for places 1-8: the places behind each, one bit each, bit 7 place 8 down to bit 0 place 1: 1 hides 4, 2 hides 5, 3 hides 6, 7 and 8, 6 hides 5, 7 hides 4, 8 hides 6 and 7.
For each of the twelve probes, its step from the party's square as a direction relative to the facing (move_relative): $80 none, 0 ahead, 1 ahead and right, 2 right, $FF ahead and left, $FE left.
For each probe, the side it looks at, relative to the facing it had ($2B51): 0 ahead, 1 right, $FF left.
The first of the three places each probe's wall hides.
The second place each probe's wall hides.
The third place each probe's wall hides.
Moves the party's square one step in direction X of eight (dir_dx, dir_dy), wrapping inside the 16 by 16 block.
The change across for the eight directions, north first and clockwise: 0, +1, +1, +1, 0, -1, -1, -1.
The change down for the eight directions: -1, -1, 0, +1, +1, +1, 0, -1.

Moves the party's square in direction A relative to the facing ($80 not at all): the direction is A plus twice the facing, used without wrapping it to 0-7. Facing north, the left-hand directions $FE and $FF read 254 and 255 bytes past dir_dx and dir_dy, in cell_paths, and both give one step north; facing west, the right-hand direction 2 reads the byte after each table and gives one step west and nine down. So some probes and places are worked out on the wrong squares.
Faces the way A gives relative to the kept facing ($2B51) and reads the wall on that side (square_info); returns it in A.

Command 12, SETUP MONSTER, also the start of ENCOUNTER MENU. Three operands: the monsters' picture ($6DD0, found or loaded by find_sprite_picture), the distance wanted ($6DC1, 0-2, or random for $80 and up, more than 2 meaning 2) and the close-up picture ($6DDA). In a 3D area the monsters are placed (place_monster) in the farthest visible place up to that distance, after cancel_back_turn and find_hidden_cells; outdoors they stand at the middle place at distance 1. Their sprites are drawn, and at distance 0, with pictures on (bit 0 of $49FF), the close-up picture is shown after a pause.

From the farthest place for distance X (farthest_place) back towards the party, takes the first place not hidden ($6DBF), walks the party's square along that place's path (cell_paths) to find the monsters' square ($6DC2/$6DC3) and sets the distance it lies at (place_distance, $6DC0); then puts the party's square back.
The farthest place for each distance: 0 for distance 0, 3 for 1, 8 for 2.
The distance of each place 0-8: 0; 1 for places 1-3; 2 for places 4-8.

Each place's path from the party's square, two directions relative to the facing ($80 no step): place 0 none, 1 ahead-left, 2 ahead-right, 3 ahead, 4 two ahead-left, 5 two ahead-right, 6 ahead then ahead-right, 7 ahead then ahead-left, 8 two ahead.
Copies the party's square, facing, wall ahead and square byte ($C04B-$C04F) to $2B4F-$2B53.
Copies them back from $2B4F-$2B53.
Command 13, APPROACH: when the monsters are not already at distance 0 ($6DC0), places them one step nearer (find_hidden_cells, place_monster).

Command 32, NEW ECL: keeps the old area's script number in $49F2; for a new one (not $FF, not the current $6E1B) marks it to be loaded ($6E1B = number with bit 7) and clears the area's 32 flags at $4A00. Then keeps the party's place, counts a restart ($6DDD), drops the stack back and starts the module again (dungeon_init), which loads it.

Command 33, LOAD FILES: the area's map number ($49C5, kept unless the first operand is $FF), the SECSET file (second operand, slot 3), then in a 3D area GEO (slot 2) by the map number, WALLS (slot 9) by the third operand and GDRIVE01; outdoors SQRDATA (slot 4) by the map number, SQRPACI (slot 1) by the third operand and GDRIVE00.
Command 37, ON GOTO: an index, a count, then that many addresses: goes to the address the index picks, or on past them all when the index is not below the count.
Command 38, ON GOSUB: as ON GOTO, but calls the address picked (from $16EF, as GOSUB) and returns after the list; nothing when the index is not below the count.
Command 39, TREASURE: seven 16-bit operands into $6EE7-$6EF4, as many as there are kinds of money, and an eighth into $6EF5; CLEAR MONSTERS empties them.

Command 40, ROB: the first operand chooses whom (0 one member at random, else everyone), the second the share of money taken in percent and the third the chance for each item. Each victim keeps (100 less the share) percent of each of the seven coins (rob_money) and loses items (rob_items); then their figures are worked out again and stored.
Robs the member in hand: money, items, combat figures, stored back.
Each of the seven coin counts ($6BBB-$6BC8, 16-bit) times the percentage kept ($6E43), over 100: hundreds and remainder ($6E3F) are scaled apart and added.

For each of the sixteen items: the chance is the third operand ($6E85), less 90 for an item weighing 256 or more ($6D85) or less 50 for one weighing 25 or more, halved when the item is readied (bit 7 of $6D82); a roll of 0-99 under it takes the item ($6D7C = 0).

Command 41, ENCOUNTER MENU: SETUP MONSTER's three operands, then the variable for the outcome, five numbers for the monsters' answer to each of the party's choices (0 attack, 1 wait, 2 flee, 3 advance, 4 parley), three texts for the distances (their places kept in $6E88 and $6E8B up), and two speeds: the one the party must beat to flee ($6E8E) and the monsters' own ($6E8F). Outdoors the monsters count as close ($6DC0 = 0). Shows the text for the distance and the menu COMBAT WAIT FLEE ADVANCE PARLAY (ADVANCE only while the monsters are not close, PARLAY only when they are), then settles the two sides' choices: an attack begins a fight (outcome 1) unless a flight succeeds (check_flight); the party fleeing gives outcome 2, the monsters fleeing 0; an advance brings the monsters a step nearer and asks again; a parley by either side gives outcome 3; waiting on both sides prints EVERYONE WAITS and asks again. The left arrow is not refused: its $FF reads the party's bits from $2403, $A0 (COMBAT and ADVANCE), and the monsters' from beyond the table.
The party's choice as a bit in the high half: COMBAT $80, WAIT 0, FLEE $40, ADVANCE $20, PARLAY $10.
The monsters' answer (0-4) as a bit in the low half: attack $08, wait 0, flee $04, advance $02, parley $01.
Stores A in the encounter menu's variable, clears the menu bar and pauses.
Prints the encounter's text for the distance, or the nearest one below that is not empty, through PRINT's word wrap; a text that is a packed string in the script is decoded first (fetch_string_at).

Whether a flight works: the party's fastest ($6E91) and slowest ($6E92) movement ($6C1B). The party gets away when its slowest is faster than the speed given ($6E8E), the monsters when they are faster than the party's fastest; on a tie it is a coin toss (random). A = 1 when the flight works.
The encounter menu bar: five items, an empty heading, then COMBAT, WAIT, FLEE, ADVANCE and PARLAY.
Command 42, GET TABLE: the byte at the first operand's address plus the second, stored in the third.
Command 53, SAVE TABLE: stores the first operand at the second operand's address plus the third.
At the module's start after a fight: when COMBAT kept a place in the script ($6DCC/$6DCD), clears it, redraws in a 3D area and runs the script on from there.

Command 44, PARLAY: asks PICK SPEAKER until a standing member is chosen ($49E3), sets the charisma's reaction figure ($6DCF, charisma_reaction by $6B19) and shows PARLAY: HAUGHTY SLY NICE MEEK ABUSIVE; the first five operands are the answers for each attitude, and the one chosen is stored in the sixth.
The parley menu bar: five items, heading "PARLAY:", then HAUGHTY, SLY, NICE, MEEK and ABUSIVE.
The speaker's reaction figure by charisma 0-25: 0 up to 3, then 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 for 4 to 8, 25 up to 12, then 30, 35, 40, 50 and on by fives to 95 at 25.

Command 45, CALL: jumps to machine code at the operand's address, with A, X and Y from $03DE-$03E0 (restore_regs), by writing the address into the JMP at $24C7; the code's RTS returns to the interpreter. The JMP's address left in the module is $BA03, sound_start.
The low byte of CALL's JMP at $24C7.
The high byte of CALL's JMP at $24C7.

Command 46, DAMAGE: five operands, how ($6E83), the dice ($6E84 count, $6E85 sides), a bonus ($6E86) and a to-hit or saving-throw figure ($6E87, bit 7 kept in $2B78: the member in hand). With bit 7 of the first clear, its low bits are a number of blows, each at a random standing member, hitting when a roll of 0-19 plus the figure reaches the target's armour class figure (hit_roll). With bit 7 set it is a saving throw (bit 5 set: none allowed), on one random member or, with bit 6, on everyone. Each victim hit, or who fails the save, loses the dice plus the bonus (apply_damage); a save avoids it all. If no one is left standing, DEATH FOR ALL is printed and the game stops in an endless loop at $2525.
Loads member $6DB4 (at $4415); carry set when it is there and neither GONE (2) nor DEAD (3).
A random member (0-7) who is standing, up to sixteen tries; carry clear when none was found. With bit 7 of $2B78 set, the member in hand at once.

Carry clear (failed) when no save is allowed ($6E41); otherwise a d20 against the member's saving throw of type $6E87 ($6B9A + type) plus the low five bits of the first operand: carry set when the roll is at least that.

A roll of 0-19 plus the figure ($6E87) against the target's armour class figure, 60 less the armour class ($6C0F, or $6C10, the rear figure, when bit 7 of $6C00 says the member is down): carry set for a hit.

On a new row: the victim's name, then the dice ($6E84 of $6E85 sides, roll_dice) plus the bonus taken from the hit points ($6C19/$6C1A). A member already at 0, or left 10 or more below 0, is DEAD ($83); one left at 0 to -9 is UNCONSIOUS ($85), and either way " IS " and the condition are printed; otherwise " IS HIT FOR " and the damage. Then a pause and the entry stored.
Hit points to 0 and " IS " (message 38) with the condition from LIBRARY's messages (41 plus the status).
Shows message X on the cleared menu bar.
Command 14, PICTURE: the operand is a close-up picture to show; $FF takes it away and redraws the view.

Shows close-up picture A: loads its files (load_picture_files); when that gives carry set (a whole picture while $6E18 is $7F or more), redraws the view instead. Otherwise sprites off, the animation stopped ($2B79 = 0, so wait_key animates it), ANIMATE loaded (slot 11) and its routines $8400 and $8403 called, then for a head and body portrait ($6DE1 not negative) $840C and $8403.
Command 47, AND: the first two operands ANDed, the flags kept for the IFs, the result in the third.
Command 48, OR: the first two operands ORed, the flags kept, the result in the third.
Command 49, and much else: all sprites off ($D015 = 0).
Command 51, PRINT RETURN: the cursor to the start of the next row, scrolling at the window's bottom.
Command 50, FIND ITEM: looks through the sixteen items of each member, last first, for one whose type's first byte ($6D8C) equals the operand; the flags kept say equal when one is found.
Command 52, CLOCK: the operand's minutes on the clock (add_minutes).

Command 54, ADD NPC: loads monster file A (MON) as a party member in the free slot below 8 ($03FD), flagged as an NPC (bit 7 of $6BB8, with the second operand halved in its low bits), $6C0C = $80, its strength index and combat figures worked out; the party list is redrawn. Without a free slot the second operand is skipped.

Command 55, LOAD PIECES: three operands, the wall sets' file numbers for slots 0-2 ($FF keeps one), each marked to load when it changes (set_wall_files); then they are loaded (load_wall_sets), the walls recoloured and the view redrawn.
Command 56, PROGRAM: sets the next module ($6E11) to the operand, keeps the party's place and drops the stack back to the linker, which loads it.

For a text whose address is in the script ($9900 and up, A its high byte): decodes the packed string there into $9700 (decode_string), keeping the instruction pointer; returns the address to print from.

Loads a close-up picture: with $6DE1 negative a whole picture, PIC (slot 5), and carry set when $6E18 is $7F or more; otherwise a portrait, BODY (slot 13, file A) and HEAD (slot 14, file $6DE1), carry clear.
Command 57, WHO: asks the question at the operand's address (choose_member) until a standing member is picked, and loads it.
Command 58, DELAY: waits as long as the message speed says ($49FC).

Command 59, SPELL: looks for spell A among the standing members' memorised spells (find_spell) and stores the place in the list (X) in the second operand and the member in the third ($FF when no one has it).
Looks for spell A in the memorised spells ($6B20-$6B70) of members 7 to 0 who are standing: returns the member in A and the place in the list in X, or A = $FF.

For a field at $6BA5-$6BAC (by its low byte), the thief's skills: works out the combat figures and, when armour is readied ($6DEC) and it is not item type 50, gives 0 instead of the skill. Other fields come back as they are.
Zeroes the working character's second page ($6C20-$6D1F) before a monster or NPC is loaded.
The text delay for PRINT ($03FC): eight times one more than the message speed ($49FC).
Keeps A (low) and X (high) as the value, $6E41/$6E42.

Command 60, PRINT GLYPHS: installs a new character set if one is waiting (then the cursor goes home), and puts the zero-terminated bytes at the operand's address on the screen as they are, screen codes in white, from the cursor, going on to the next row at the window's right edge.
Command 61, CLEAR BOX: the text window set to the view's inside (clear_box_edges) and cleared.
The window CLEAR BOX clears: columns 1 to 16, rows 1 to 16.
Keeps A (low) and X (high) in $6E43/$6E44.
Starts a loop over the party at member 7 ($6DB4).
For wall set $2B70: when file A (not $FF) differs from the set's WALLSET ($6E22 + set) or WALLDEF ($6E25 + set) number, stores it with bit 7 set, to be loaded.

Shows the monsters' picture found by find_sprite_picture ($9713/$9714): its two sprite colours ($9700/$9701 into $D025/$D026), then the images for the distance $6DC0 (the picture holds a set for each, $9708-$970A images long) as sprites 1 up: each image's pointer ($60 + its number, at $CFF8 + sprite), colour and multicolour bit (its byte at $ED00), and place, from the picture's offsets for that distance (outdoors fixed), mirrored as 254 less the offset, shifted across for the place ($6DBF, sprite_offsets), plus $30 across and $4A down. No sprite is expanded or past column 255; the sprites used are turned on ($D015, from bit_masks).
How far across each of the nine places is shifted: 0, -25, +20, 0, -32, +33, +33, -32, 0.
Copies the first twelve bytes of the picture entry at $9E/$9F to $9700 with all 64 KB RAM showing.
load_sprite_picture's working bytes: where the images go, low byte ($2A17) and high byte ($2A18): $D800 plus $300 per entry.
The high byte of where load_sprite_picture puts the images.
Where load_sprite_picture puts each image's colour byte: $ED00 plus this.
Images left to copy in load_sprite_picture (twelve).

Finds picture $6DD0 among the pictures held under the KERNAL: six entries of $40 bytes at $EA00, their header's byte $0B the picture's number ($6D79 how many there are). When it is not there, loads it (load_sprite_picture) into the next entry ($6D7A), round again to entry 0 after the sixth (entry 1 outdoors, so entry 0 stays), and looks again. Leaves the entry's address in $9713/$9714 and its first image's number in $970C.

Loads SPRITE file $6DD0 (slot 10, at $8400) into entry $6D7A: its 64-byte header, with the picture's number put in byte $0B, to $EA00 + $40 per entry, its twelve images to $D800 + $300 per entry and each image's last byte, its colour, to $ED00 + 12 per entry. With all 64 KB RAM showing.
Copies X bytes and then Y more pages from the address in $2B2B/$2B2C to the one in $2B2E/$2B2F, by changing its own LDA and STA.
block_copy's LDA address, low byte ($2B2C high): where the copy reads.
The high byte of block_copy's source.
block_copy's STA address, low byte ($2B2F high): where the copy writes.
The high byte of block_copy's destination.
The Adventure Menu's cursor place, kept while a command runs. $2B48-$2B4E are not used by this module.
save_position's copy of the party's square across ($2B4F), down ($2B50), facing ($2B51), wall ahead and square byte; also the party's own square for draw_area_map and match_c04b.
The kept facing (saved_position + 2), which turn_and_look turns from.
draw_area_map's square: its north and east walls as two bits, then the character drawn.
Where the AREA map stops across (map_end_x) and, at $2B56, down.
Where the AREA map stops down. $2B57-$2B5B are not used.
fit_word's room left on the row. $2B5D-$2B5F are not used.
Which of its three images the overland marker shows, 0-2.
